question: A 56-year-old man presents seeking treatment for his baldness. He says he has noticed a bald patch in the center of his head which has increased in size over the past year. Physical examination and diagnostic tests show no evidence of an infectious cause. The patient is prescribed a drug be taken daily. After 4 months, the patient returns for follow-up and says that his hair growth has increased significantly. He denies any significant side effects except for a slight decrease in his sex drive. Which of the following is most likely the mechanism of action of the drug this patient was prescribed?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Drug prescribed" -> "Inhibits 5α reductase enzyme" -> "Reduces conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT)" -> "Decreased DHT levels lead to hair growth" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Drug prescribed" -> "Blocks androgen receptors" -> "Prevents binding of DHT to receptors in hair follicles" -> "Promotes hair growth" -> 90%
analysis: The drug prescribed to the patient most likely works by inhibiting the enzyme 5α reductase, which is involved in the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). By reducing DHT levels, the drug can promote hair growth. The side effect of decreased sex drive is a known potential side effect of 5α reductase inhibitors.
